description: The healthcheck 'give up' path never invokes self-fix.sh directly; it only writes a static selfheal-request.json and returns, relying on a future SUCCESSFUL launch of the very loop session that is currently failing to launch. If the root cause is in the launch mechanism itself (broken $CLAUDE path, corrupted cli.sh, tmux socket/permission failure) rather than something only reachable from inside a running claude turn, there is no code path that ever spawns an Opus dev to fix the launcher -- the note simply sits unread forever.

evidence.snippet:
if [ "$count" -ge 5 ]; then echo "$(date '+%F %T') backoff $count/60min — delegating to loop" >> "$LOG"
    if [ ! -f "$REQ" ] || [ "$(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -f %m "$REQ" 2>/dev/null||echo 0) ))" -gt 3600 ]; then
      printf '{"loop":"capafy", ... "note":"healthcheck gave up. Next wake: diagnose+fix yourself, verify, rm this; else self/issue-dev then rm."}\n' ... > "$REQ" 2>/dev/null; fi; return; fi

concreteFailureScenario: capafy-loop-cli.sh gets corrupted (e.g. a bad edit breaks its bash syntax) so every tmux new-session invocation exits immediately. Healthcheck restarts it 5 times within an hour, hits backoff, writes the note, and 'delegates to loop' -- but the loop can never launch to read that note. This is identical across all three loops (life-manager-loop-healthcheck.sh:14-16, reddit-loop-healthcheck.sh:14) since it is a copy-pasted pattern.
